findings.title: refund() no longer rejects unpaid orders
findings.rationale: Per the diff description, the `if (!order.paid) throw` guard was removed from refund(). Nothing in refund() now checks that the order was paid before refunding it. This is an unverified claim: I could not open pay.js or the diff in this session, so I have not confirmed the surrounding code.
findings.failure_scenario: An order with paid=false (never captured, or payment failed) is passed to refund(). The refund goes through and money is returned for a charge that never settled, or a refund is issued on an order that is already refunded or partially paid. Any caller that relied on refund() to enforce the paid check now gets no protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the guard at the top of refund() (`if (!order.paid) throw ...`), or, if the check moved elsewhere, confirm every call path to refund() enforces it. Add a test that refund() on an unpaid order throws.
